decisions.decision_value: Limit production costs to 12.5 Euros per unit with a 25 Euro selling price
decisions.rationale: Financial targets set at kick-off meeting.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: We're looking at um having our production costs limited to uh twelve and an half Euro per unit.

decisions.decision_value: TV-only remote control without teletext, incorporating corporate colour and slogan
decisions.rationale: Internet makes teletext obsolete and corporate branding is mandatory.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: whatever device we come up with at the end of the day had to incorporate um the corporate colour and slogan.

decisions.decision_value: First planned to let people find a lost remote using a keyring-style hand-clap / whistle-back sound detector (specifically a clap option so everyone can use it)
decisions.rationale: Louisa (C) suggested a whistle-back or clap keyring locator; Robin (D) and Alastair (A) chose clapping over whistling because more people can clap than whistle.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I would have thought that more people could clap rather than whistle, so uh so clap option.

decisions.decision_value: Keep main controls on top and hide secondary tuning/brightness/contrast buttons under a slide-down panel
decisions.rationale: Avoids cluttering the main face while preserving access to infrequently used settings.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: have you seen those remotes where kind of um the bottom bit slides down, so there's kind of um everything else revealed?

decisions.decision_value: Use kinetic energy (shake/movement-powered) to power the remote
decisions.rationale: Eliminates replacement batteries and fits innovative branding.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I thought possibly for power we could use kinetic um which is the idea of the watches um that you move you move the remote around to power it up.

decisions.decision_value: Changed lost-remote plan from hand-clap/whistle detector to programmable voice/speech recognition (recording a spoken prompt like 'Where are you remote?' and getting a spoken reply like 'Here I am, Jo')
decisions.rationale: The company already manufactured a programmable voice recognition sample sensor/speaker chip (from its coffee machines) that responds to a recorded call phrase.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: It might be useful to say like where are you remote. Here I am, Jo. But I think that's maybe as far as that one could go?

decisions.decision_value: User Interface Designer (Louisa, Speaker C) suggested presenting/marketing the voice recognition to buyers specifically as a 'finder function' for finding a lost remote rather than competing on voice-operated TV functions
decisions.rationale: Leading competitors already had full-function voice-recognition remotes, whereas their chip only responds to a recorded phrase, making it ideal to market as a dedicated 'finder function'.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: because ours might not cover the same functions that the leading brands do, it might be a good idea to market it as a um finder function.

decisions.decision_value: Single-curved standard rubber case with standard rubber push-buttons
decisions.rationale: Chosen for durability and soft texture.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: it seems to make sense that we we'd just maybe stick with the standard rubber case, and then have the standard rubber buttons as well.

decisions.decision_value: Changed case material from rubber to plastic to reduce prototype cost from 13.7 Euros down to 12.3 Euros (under the 12.5 Euro budget)
decisions.rationale: Initial prototype cost was 13.7 Euros; switching from a rubber case to a plastic case saved 2 Euros while keeping kinetic power, voice recognition finder, and fruit-shaped buttons at 12.3 Euros.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Oh actually we just have a plastic case, then we lose two points, which gets us

action_items.resolution_summary: Louisa (C) and Nick (B) reported on the programmable coffee-machine speech recognition unit in ES2014c and Louisa proposed marketing it as a finder function.
